messages:
sam-sales: Kicking off BankTheta Private POC. They need: literal client src IP in logs (for audit), one static egress IP for their firewall, and compatibility with an inline TLS-inspect appliance. They also attached a compliance pack. Can eng outline options + a minimal netops checklist?
irina-net: Short list of topologies: (1) Routed VPC peering/transit 1:1 preserves L3 src IP. Requires route exchange and acceptance of our ASN on their side. (2) PrivateLink + customer-side egress proxy that NATs to single IP and emits a signed header with original IP. (3) Dedicated connector VM in customer's VPC that forwards traffic untouched.
devin-se: PrivateLink is lowest-friction. If they insist on network-layer src IP, peering is the only reliable option without introducing headers. If they can accept app-layer evidence, we recommend signed header: X-Orig-Client-IP + X-Orig-Client-IP-Sig (HMAC-SHA256).
maria-arch: Proposed HMAC flow: customer proxy computes sig = HMAC_SHA256(key, "<ts>|<client-ip>|<request-id>") and sets headers. Our ingress verifies sig and persists both header and verification result to immutable audit logs. We can timestamp verification and include it in attestation.
irina-net: Practical netops checklist (pasteable):
- Provision proxy host (EC2/container) in customer VPC or use existing egress appliance
- If PrivateLink: create interface endpoint and restrict SG to proxy host
- Firewall: allow outbound to Redwood ENI(s) on TCP/443 (or public IPs if not using PrivateLink)
- Proxy: add headers X-Orig-Client-IP and X-Orig-Client-IP-Sig (HMAC_SHA256). Rotate HMAC key via KMS and share verification key securely (or use signed JWKS flow)
- Healthchecks: open TCP 8080 for our health probes from eng-oncall CIDR
- MTU: ensure 1500 or tune MSS for IPSec/SD-WAN paths
- DNS/NTP: allow corporate resolver and NTP (UDP 123)
devin-se: Sample firewall allowlist (public egress):
```
203.0.113.10/32 TCP 443 (redwood-ingress-a)
203.0.113.11/32 TCP 443 (redwood-ingress-b)
NTP UDP 123 to corp NTP
DNS TCP/UDP 53 to corp resolver
```
If using PrivateLink: instead lock SGs to ENI IPs returned by our onboarding playbook.
maria-arch: Security notes: E2E TLS to Redwood preferred. If TLS-inspect terminates and re-encrypts, feature caveats: function-calling or client-cert pinning may fail. Need customer to list which features they rely on.
legalbot: We can provide a scoped attestation for the POC: "Redwood verifies HMAC on X-Orig-Client-IP and records headers and verification outcome in immutable logs for the POC window." Approval required from security/legal; customer must document KMS custody and rotation.
\sam-sales: Pricing: does a dedicated connector cost extra?
irina-net: Yes, connector/appliance is an add-on (onboarding + monthly infra + egress billing). PrivateLink-only POC is cheaper but may not meet literal src IP requirement. Devin: can you draft a 30-day POC estimate?
devin-se: On it 1 I'll include a minimal connector SKU and PrivateLink-only SKU.
sam-sales: Customer wants the handoff doc (diagram + checklist + proxy env vars + attestation draft) by EOD tomorrow. Can we do that?
oncall-bot: Reminder created: ticket POC-1122 assigned to eng-oncall for network onboarding and connectivity tests.
sam-sales: Thanks all 1 will consolidate and send to customer once handoff ready :thumbsup:
